newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-WORLD CUP RETURNS TO BRECKENRIDGE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WORLD CUP RETURNS TO BRECKENRIDGE.

text.p: Little can be known for certain of a World Cup ski season after just three races, but some things may be surmised.

Foremost, the men of Austria own a franchise in the technical events, particularly slalom. Another presumption is that Michael Von Gruenigen of Switzerland is as consistently good as ever in giant slalom.
A third observation concerns the apparent difficulty for male World Cup champions to retain their titles, as evidenced by the early season lapse of Lasse Kjus of Norway.

Each of these themes will receive a postscript here Saturday and Sunday, when giant slalom and slalom races echo a programme held here in 1991, the only other time this Colorado resort hosted the alpine World Cup.
Breckenridge boasts uncommonly good early snowfall and courses are firmly prepared on variable terrain with short, steep pitches that form a keen test of concentration.

In building a commanding Nations Cup lead, Austria already demonstrated a slalom dominance with a 1-2 finish by Thomas Sykora and Thomas Stangassinger last Sunday at Park City, Utah. Austria also got a Utah victory from Josef Strobl in giant slalom.

Steve Locher of Switzerland won the season opening giant slalom in late October on the glacier at Soelden, Austria, but his teammate, Von Gruenigen, has been the hallmark of stability. The defending GS champion, Von Gruenigen has finished third in both races and again leads that standing with 140 points, 10 ahead of Austria's Hans Knaus, 14 up on Locher.
Von Gruenigen also has designs on the overall title. Third last season, he has the early lead with 154 points. Kjetil Andre Aamodt of Norway, the 1994 champion, trails closely with 136.
This failure of once-dominant racers like Aamodt to repeat as overall champion has become a prevailing theme.

Not since Pirmin Zurbriggen of Switzerland in 1988 has a male racer defended his overall title. Kjus, who won for the first time last season, may be destined to continue the trend. Skiing off course in the first two races, he showed none of the determination that took him to the title.

Again, Italian star Alberto Tomba will be missing from the field, electing to nurse an injured wrist at home while preparing for his debut at a December 17 slalom before his countrymen at Madonna di Campiglio.
